19.0.s.en: (1) The Levite brings back his concubine

19.0.0.en: When there was no king: that is, in the age of the judges, before the age of the kings began.

19.0.1.en: The sides of mount Ephraim: "sides" is the plural of a word meaning a high place, that is, the high places in the hill country of Ephraim.

19.0.2.en: From this verse to the end of the book, the inspired text tells us another story that also happened in the time of the judges, which gives us a picture of the extent of the spiritual decline and of the spread of fornication among the people of God, so that it almost destroyed an entire tribe, the tribe of Benjamin.

19.0.3.en: The story here is about a man of the Levites who was living temporarily on one edge of the land of Ephraim, and who had taken a maidservant as a wife, which the ancient Law permitted, and she was from Bethlehem.

19.1.0.en: That maidservant fell into the sin of fornication and feared that she would be punished by stoning according to the Law, so she fled to Bethlehem, to her father's home, and stayed with him four months.

19.2.0.en: To speak friendly unto her: to speak to her kindly and win her consent.

19.2.1.en: With the passing of time she repented and was sorry, so her husband forgave her for her fault and went to her father's house to reconcile with her and show her that he had put her deed out of mind. The woman welcomed him and brought him into her father's house, and her father also rejoiced when he learned that he had come to reconcile with his wife.

19.3.0.en: To show his welcome to him, her father asked him to accept his hospitality for several days, and he stayed with him three days, during which he honored him.

19.4.0.en: A morsel of bread: a humble expression of the host, by which he means eating a meal.

19.4.1.en: On the morning of the fourth day, since the Levite was about to depart, he rose early in preparation for leaving, taking his wife with him, but her father asked him to wait a little until he could give him enough food to help him with the hardship of the journey so that he would not be weary on the way.

19.5.0.en: The Levite accepted his father-in-law's invitation, and the two sat together and ate, and as he was leaving, his father-in-law held on to him and asked him to stay with him another night, so that they might converse in the evening and enjoy being together.

19.6.0.en: The Levite had resolved to depart, but his father-in-law held him and urged him to stay another night.

19.7.0.en: The guest rose early on the morning of the fifth day to take his wife and leave his father-in-law's house, but his father-in-law again urged him anew to stay and eat, for there was no reason for such haste, and to wait until after noon. The Levite was compelled to accept his father-in-law's invitation, so he sat and ate.

19.8.0.en: When the time to depart came again, and the Levite, his wife, and his servant were about to go, his father-in-law said to him that the day was declining and that it was not right to begin their journey at that late hour of the day, so let him stay this night also, lest night fall upon them on the road and they be exposed to dangers, and he promised him that when the night passed he would let him leave early in the morning to return to his dwelling place.

19.9.0.en: This time the Levite did not yield to his father-in-law's request and insisted on leaving. He went on his way until he came to a place near Jebus (Jerusalem), and with him were his concubine, his servant, and his two asses with saddles and riding gear.

19.9.1.en: How good it is to honor our guests so that they feel comfortable and at ease in being with us, knowing that God honors us if we honor others, but let it be done with wisdom, so that we do not hinder them from their work and responsibilities.

19.10.0.en: Jebus: the city that was afterward called Jerusalem.

19.10.1.en: The Levite left Bethlehem and went on his way until he came to the city of Jebus, which is about 9 km from Bethlehem. The Jebusites, the original inhabitants of the land, were still living in it. The Levite's servant who worked for him said to his master, "Let us lodge in Jebus, for the night has come."

19.11.0.en: Gibeah: a city north of Jerusalem (Map 10). The Levite did not agree to his servant's proposal because the people of Jebus were not Israelites, that is, they were strangers to him, and he saw that it was more fitting to go on a little farther until they reached the town of "Gibeah," one of the cities of the tribe of Benjamin.

19.12.0.en: Ramah: a village 8 km north of Jerusalem.

19.12.1.en: The Levite urged his servant to continue until they reached a place where the children of Israel lived, such as "Gibeah" or "Ramah," and spend their night there.

19.13.0.en: They did go on until they reached the town of Gibeah, where the tribe of Benjamin lived, and they arrived after the sun had set and night had come.

19.14.0.en: They entered the city to spend the night in it and came to a wide square at the entrance of the city. Everyone who passed by the place saw them, but no one invited them to lodge with him. This shows the bad character of the people of the city, for there was no one who cared to take in this stranger, because they were selfish, caring only for their own pleasures.

19.15.0.en: They stayed in the place until an old man of the town passed by, who was originally of the tribe of Ephraim but was living in Gibeah temporarily. He was returning from his work in the field to his house, and he saw the Levite, his concubine, and his servant sitting in the square, so he came and asked them where they had come from and where they were going.

19.16.0.en: The Levite answered the old man that they had left Bethlehem for the sides of the hill country of Ephraim, where they lived. He was going to the house of the Lord at "Shiloh," which is about 27 km north of Jerusalem.

19.17.0.en: The Levite made clear that he would not burden the one who took him in with anything but a place to sleep. They had everything they needed of food and drink and provender for the asses, so their lodging would not be a burden on their host.

19.18.0.en: The old man said to him, "Do not say so, for I will take care of all your needs of food and drink, for this is the duty of hospitality, so come with me to my house and leave the city square."

19.19.0.en: They accepted the old man's invitation and came with him to his house, where he honored them and gave provender to their asses, and they washed their feet, and he gave them food and drink, and they ate and drank and rested at his house.

19.19.1.en: Be reassured if you live or deal with selfish or wicked people, for God will not leave you alone but makes with the temptation a way of escape, sending you someone who cares for you and solves your problems.

19.20.s.en: (3) The rape and death of the concubine

19.20.0.en: As they were making their hearts merry: rejoicing in eating and drinking and rest after the day's weariness.

19.20.1.en: Men of Belial: wicked men, sons of Satan, for Belial is the name of a pagan god, called the god of the night.

19.20.2.en: Bring forth the man that came into thine house, that we may know him: bring out the man that we may commit fornication with him.

19.20.3.en: While they were sitting conversing after the toil of the journey, a group of wicked men of the city gathered before the old man's house, beating hard on his door, demanding that he hand over his guest to them so that they could commit perversion and sin with him.

19.21.0.en: The master of the house objected to the wicked men gently so that they would not abuse his guest, and offered them to hand over to them his virgin daughter and the man's concubine to commit fornication with them. This is of course a wrong solution, but it seems that at this time the position of woman was low in the eyes of society, and this offer was an attempt by the host to deliver the Levite from their hand.

19.21.1.en: A similar story happened in the book of Genesis, the story of Lot when the wicked attacked his house to abuse the two men he had taken in, who were the two angels (Gen 19), but the situation here is harder because the wicked are of the people of God and not pagans like the people of Sodom.

19.22.0.en: The wicked men did not respond to the entreaties of the master of the house and insisted on their demand, so the Levite guest had no choice but to bring his concubine out to them, handing her over to their hand. They took her and committed fornication with her all night long, enjoying their evil desires, and then they let her go in the morning.

19.23.0.en: The concubine went from the hand of the wicked men and came to the old man's house where her lord the Levite was, and she was in great exhaustion, so she fell down before the house until the sun rose.

19.24.0.en: The Levite rose in the morning to return to his country, having lost his concubine, since he thought that the men of Gibeah would not give back the concubine, and he was startled to find his concubine fallen at the door of the house with her hands stretched out toward the door, perhaps because she had wanted to knock on it and could not for extreme weariness.

19.25.0.en: The Levite thought she was asleep and called to her, trying to wake her to continue the journey with him, but she had departed this life. So the man loaded her body on his ass and returned with her to his house on the edges of Ephraim.

19.25.1.en: This concubine had been living quietly with her lord and husband the Levite, but she was negligent and committed fornication, and God allowed the gravity of fornication to be shown in that those wicked men raped her and were the cause of her death. So do not be negligent with sin, even with a small negligence, lest your immersion in it increase and you bring many evils upon yourself and become a cause of your own destruction.

19.26.0.en: Shock and grief drove the Levite to a harsh thought, which was to cut the concubine's body into twelve pieces and send them to the twelve tribes, in order to show them how monstrous was what the Gibeonites had done to him, and to ask their judgment and verdict in this matter.

19.27.0.en: Everyone of the children of Israel who saw and heard was astonished and disgusted at this vile deed, the like of which had not happened since they came out of the land of Egypt to this day. And they considered the matter, how they would face this great evil.

19.27.1.en: The war between the tribe of Benjamin and the rest of the tribes

20.0.0.en: The story of the rape of the Levite's concubine shook the conscience of the people, so the men of Israel from all the tribes assembled, from the north where Dan is to the south where Beer-sheba is, and from the east also, where Gilead is. They all gathered before the house of the Lord and the ark of His covenant, which they had moved from Shiloh to Mizpeh. They gathered in the name of the Lord to present their matter to Him.

20.1.0.en: Footmen: those who walk, that is, a huge company of infantry.

20.1.1.en: That drew sword: fit to use swords in war.

20.1.2.en: The chiefs of the people and the leading figures of all the tribes stood in the assembly the people held to consider this vile matter committed by a group of wicked men, and the number of those assembled was four hundred thousand footmen able to bear arms.

20.2.0.en: Tell us, how was this wickedness?: they asked everyone who knew anything about this dreadful event and this vile deed.

20.2.1.en: Benjamin learned of the assembly the tribes held at Mizpeh, but they did not try to set right their position. The chiefs of the people who were present asked the Levite and those who knew him to present the vile story to the tribes.

20.3.0.en: The Levite began to speak, since he was the first concerned in the matter, and he described what had happened from the time he entered the house of his host in Gibeah to spend the night with him.

20.4.0.en: A company of the people of the city attacked the house and wanted to commit perversion with him, so he handed over his concubine to them, fearing for his life, and they assaulted her in a savage manner until she departed this life from extreme exhaustion.

20.5.0.en: The Levite was gravely shocked by this barbarous act, so he decided to inform all the children of Israel so that they might judge his case. He cut his concubine's body into 12 pieces and sent them to all the territories of Israel so that they might judge this heinous crime.

20.6.0.en: "And here you represent all the tribes of the children of Israel; judge in this case of mine and give your opinion on this dreadful tragedy."

20.6.1.en: If you face a problem, bring it to the priests and servants responsible in the Church to judge it, and do not act by yourself in anger, lest you sin. Lift up your heart in prayer, consult your father of confession, wait for God's guidance to you, and know that your God is just and strong, and no matter escapes Him.

20.7.s.en: (2) Benjamin refuses to hand over the criminals

20.7.0.en: Those assembled decided with one mind that no one should leave his place in this great assembly and that none of them should return to his dwelling place until they had examined the story and judged it, and they decided to ask God and cast lots to choose who would fight against Gibeah and who would provide for the needs of the fighters.

20.8.1.en: Those assembled also decided to divide the men of each tribe into ten parts and to choose one part of them, that is, a tenth, to return to its place and bring food and the needs of war, while the rest would remain ready to fight Gibeon if it did not submit to them, and to chastise it for the evil it had done.

20.9.0.en: The men of the tribes advanced, united in one opinion, to fight Gibeon.

20.10.0.en: Before fighting Gibeah, they sent to the families of the tribe of Benjamin asking them to hand over the wicked men who had committed the crime, but they refused in pride.

20.10.1.en: Be understanding if you have erred and confess your error, and even accept the punishment if all agree on it, in order to be reconciled with those you have wronged and to submit to the opinion of the community. Then the just God will be pleased with you, and you will save yourself from many evils and calm the anger of those around you, and you will be able to win them over as time passes.

20.11.s.en: (3) The first and second battles and the defeat of the children of Israel

20.11.0.en: The tribe of Benjamin did not submit to the decision of the tribes, and after their refusal to hand over the wicked men, they prepared to fight them, so all the men of Benjamin gathered at Gibeah. It would have been better for them to apologize for their sin and not rely on their military strength; but their pride and their reliance on their strength caused much trouble and almost wiped out their tribe entirely.

20.12.0.en: The number of Benjamin's men who went into the war from their various cities was 26 thousand, in addition to 700 warriors from the city of Gibeah itself, chosen for their courage in wars and their physical abilities.

20.13.0.en: Lefthanded: men who use their left hand instead of the right.

20.13.1.en: The sling: a weapon of war like a slingshot for throwing stones to great distances.

20.13.2.en: At an hair breadth: they hit any target accurately, even if it was a hair.

20.13.3.en: Among those chosen for the war from the children of Benjamin were seven hundred who used their left hand, yet they hit the most exact targets from a long distance without missing, that is, they were very skilled in war and in using its tools in that time.

20.14.0.en: Against the men of Benjamin, four hundred thousand men of war who drew the sword gathered from the tribes of Israel to fight the tribe of Benjamin.

20.15.0.en: The army of the tribes assembled at Bethel on the border of the tribe of Benjamin, where the ark of the covenant of God and the tabernacle of meeting had been moved (v. 27), and they asked the Lord which of them should be at the head of the army and take the command (they asked by the Urim and Thummim, as was the custom). The Lord answered them that the one to be in front was the tribe of Judah. It would have been better for them to ask God first whether they should fight or not. Then God allowed them to be defeated the first two times to show them that they were all sinners and not only the tribe of Benjamin. And when they were chastened and returned to God, He allowed them victory the third time, in appreciation of their prayers, their consulting God, and their repentance, as will appear in the following verses.

20.16.0.en: On the day after they asked the Lord, the army of the tribes advanced toward Gibeah, the sinful city, and made their camp on the border of the city and made ready to fight the army that the tribe of Benjamin had prepared.

20.17.0.en: The tribe of Benjamin was victorious, and they killed 22 thousand of the tribes.

20.18.0.en: Despite the defeat of the tribes, their resolve and their desire to root out evil did not weaken. They did not despair but returned and organized their ranks anew and drew up for battle in the same place before Gibeah, as they had done the day before.

20.18.1.en: The believer must not despair if he is defeated some times in his spiritual war against Satan, but must not retreat, rather persevere and strive, and the Lord gives him strength and victory. We must always remember that loss of hope is the great sin that leaves no room for repentance and return to God.

20.19.0.en: The children of Israel turned to the Lord and wept before Him all day in sorrow for those of them who had fallen the day before, and they prayed to Him, seeking His will as to whether He was pleased for them to go back to fight the children of Benjamin again or to stop. They called the tribe of Benjamin "my brother" despite the estrangement and the dispute, because in spite of this it is indeed one of the twelve tribes of Israel. The Lord answered them to go up against him.

20.20.0.en: The soldiers of the children of Israel moved forward to meet the children of Benjamin on the day after their prayer to the Lord.

20.21.0.en: On the same day the army of Benjamin advanced toward them to fight them, and the children of Benjamin were victorious also in this second battle and killed 18 thousand soldiers of the tribes, all bearing the sword.

20.21.1.en: God allowed the defeat of the tribes twice although they had prayed and He had agreed with them to fight Gibeah, for the following reasons:

20.21.2.en: 1- So that the tribes would not become proud, feeling their strength, and kill their brethren cruelly with hearts full of evil, but He wanted them to be humbled, to know that victory would come from God.

20.21.3.en: 2- Perhaps He wanted to purify the tribes of the evil in them, such as the idol worship, an example of which is what the tribe of Dan did (ch. 18).

20.21.4.en: 3- To give the tribe of Benjamin a chance to repent and turn back from its evil.

20.22.s.en: (4) The defeat of Benjamin and the killing of its men

20.22.0.en: Bethel: a city north of Jerusalem, lying between it and Nablus.

20.22.1.en: The children of Israel grieved over their defeat twice and over the killing of great numbers of them, so the soldiers and the rest of the people went to Bethel and humbled themselves with fasting and weeping before the ark of the covenant, seeking the mercies of the Lord and His intervention to solve their problem. In atonement for their sins they offered burnt offerings, and to express their thanks to the Lord in all circumstances they offered peace offerings. These sacrifices signify Christ the Redeemer, through whom we gain victory over the demons.

20.23.0.en: The ark of the covenant in those days was at Bethel, and the high priest was Phinehas, who ministered before the ark. The children of Israel asked the Lord by way of the high priest, by vision or by the Thummim and Urim, whether they should cease fighting the children of Benjamin or face them a third time. The Lord commanded them to fight the children of Benjamin and promised them that He would give them victory in that battle on the morrow.

20.24.0.en: Israel set liers in wait round about Gibeah: that is, he set an ambush around Gibeah.

20.24.1.en: The children of Israel began to lay a plan for the war, to place an ambush of their men around Gibeah, whose task was to enter the city after the army of Benjamin came out of it to meet the children of Israel, and to burn it with fire, which was in fact carried out, as will come in the rest of the verses.

20.25.0.en: For the third time the soldiers of the children of Israel drew up facing Gibeah, as they had done in the first and second confrontations.

20.26.0.en: Were drawn away from the city: moved away from the city.

20.26.1.en: The army of the children of Benjamin came out of the city to meet the army of the children of Israel, and in this was a preparation for what the children of Israel had planned, to draw the army of the children of Benjamin away from the city. Indeed the army of the children of Israel deliberately distributed its companies on several roads so that the army of Benjamin would be scattered behind them, and more than that, they pretended to be defeated in order to encourage the enemy army to go farther and farther from the city, so that the ambush surrounding Gibeah and behind it, of the children of Israel, could enter the city and burn it. Indeed the army of Benjamin came out behind the tribes of Israel on two roads, one leading to Bethel and the other in the wilderness around Gibeah. The total of the men of the army of Israel who were killed in this pursuit was only thirty men.

20.27.0.en: The children of Benjamin were deceived by their previous victories and thought that the retreat of the children of Israel was nothing but a third defeat that would strike them. The children of Israel, however, continued to carry out their plans of drawing the army of Benjamin after them away from the city, pretending to flee and be defeated, and their plan was to scatter them more and more until they grew tired and confused, so that the ambush could enter the city without hindrance.

20.28.0.en: The soldiers of the army of Israel gathered at "Baal-tamar," a place near Gibeah, and at the same time the ambush came out of its hiding place in the wilderness of Gibeah, entering the city.

20.29.0.en: They knew not that evil was near them: they did not feel that they were in danger.

20.29.1.en: Other fighting companies joined the army of the children of Israel, their number estimated at ten thousand valiant fighters, and a fierce battle took place. The Benjamites thought they were victorious as in the previous times and did not appreciate the weakness of their position and the strength of their enemies.

20.30.0.en: The children of Israel were victorious over the Benjamites, and the victory was from the Lord, and in this battle 25,100 soldiers of the children of Benjamin were killed, all of them strong in fighting.

20.31.0.en: And the children of Israel gave place to the Benjamites: they fell back before Benjamin to draw them away from Gibeah in order to give the ambush an opportunity according to the plan laid down.

20.31.1.en: When this great number of the army of Benjamin was killed, they were sure that they had been defeated this time before the army of the tribes, although the children of Israel continued to pretend to fall back in order to draw the children of Benjamin away from the city, to give the ambush the opportunity to carry out the plan laid down.

20.31.2.en: It was pride that drove the tribe of Benjamin to come out behind the army of the tribes and move away from the city, so God allowed it to be defeated because of its pride. So do not rely on your previous successes and become proud, but give the glory to God and examine your affairs before Him in prayer and humility, and He will guide you and you will remain victorious over the devil, for by humility and holding fast to God you remain steadfast in Him and trample all the powers of evil.

20.32.0.en: The way was indeed cleared for the ambush to carry out the plan, for the children of Israel succeeded in drawing the children of Benjamin away from the city and occupied them with pursuing them, so the ambush entered the city and killed everyone in it.

20.33.0.en: There was an agreement between the soldiers of Israel and the men of the ambush that when they entered the city and destroyed those in it, they would burn it so that the smoke of the fire would rise, as a sign of the full carrying out and success of the plan.

20.34.0.en: Here is a repetition of what was mentioned before in (v. 31), that from the beginning of the battle, when Benjamin saw the (planned) retreat of the children of Israel, they thought they were fleeing, so they pursued them and killed thirty men of them.

20.35.0.en: The smoke from the burning of the city rose, which the men of the ambush carried out after entering it, and went up to heaven, and when the children of Benjamin looked behind them, they saw the whole city burning.

20.36.0.en: The children of Israel turned to advance toward Gibeah after having pretended to withdraw in the other direction, in application of the plan they had laid. Meanwhile the soldiers of Benjamin began to be terrified by the burning of their city and the attack of the army of Israel upon them, so they began to flee from before the children of Israel, after they were sure that they were defeated this time.

20.37.0.en: And them which came out of the cities they destroyed in the midst of them: the soldiers of the children of Israel who had stayed behind from taking part in the war because they were assigned to protective duties inside the cities came out to join their brethren and killed the fleeing soldiers of Benjamin.

20.37.1.en: The children of Benjamin turned back, but not toward their city because they saw it burning, so they began to flee into the wilderness around it, while the army of the tribes pursued them in every direction, and at the same time the men of the ambush who had taken their city came out against them from the other side, so both parties surrounded them from both directions and they fell dead in their midst, in addition to the soldiers of Israel coming out from their cities and killing those fleeing of the tribe of Benjamin.

20.38.0.en: The armies of Israel surrounded the children of Benjamin and pursued them while they were defeated and trying to escape, and the armies overtook them to the east of the city of Gibeah.

20.39.0.en: Vast numbers of the men of the children of Benjamin fell in this battle and terrible pursuit, for the number of their dead reached 18 thousand valiant warriors.

20.40.0.en: Gidom: a town between Gibeah and the rock of Rimmon.

20.40.1.en: They pursued hard after them: they chased them.

20.40.2.en: The children of Benjamin tried to find a gap through which they could escape from the pursuit, so they headed for a fortified place near their town called "the rock of Rimmon," but on the road they took in their flight five thousand of them were killed, whom the men of the tribes picked off easily and killed. And those who tried to escape and went farther on the road of flight, the men of the children of Israel followed them and pursued them zealously and killed two thousand more of them.

20.41.0.en: The approximate number of the dead of that battle from the tribe of Benjamin was 25 thousand sword-bearing valiant men.

20.42.0.en: Six hundred men of the tribe of Benjamin were able to save themselves by reaching the fortress called "the rock of Rimmon." They hid in it among its caves and remained hidden about four months until what will be mentioned in the next chapter happened.

20.42.1.en: It is noted that the number of the soldiers of the tribe of Benjamin was 26 thousand soldiers (v. 15), of whom 25,100 were killed (vv. 44-46) and 600 soldiers hid at "the rock of Rimmon," and there remained 300 soldiers who fell in the first and second battles and, because of their small number, were not mentioned, so that by this all the soldiers of Benjamin were killed, approximately.

20.43.0.en: After the army of Benjamin collapsed, all the cities in which the families of their tribe lived became a target for the fury of the children of Israel, who entered the land of Benjamin and killed everyone they met, even the beasts, and burned all their cities. By this the tribe almost became extinct entirely, had it not been for the success of the six hundred men who took refuge in "the rock of Rimmon" in saving themselves and remaining alive.

20.43.1.en: The tribe of Benjamin faces extinction
